messages:
maria: hey team — sudden family thing, I need someone to cover primary for the EU->APAC late window this weekend (Sat+Sun nights, roughly 20:30-04:30 UTC). I’m still on for the weekday shifts. there’s a planned model rollout Sat 22:00 UTC that I'd normally own. sorry for the short notice :disappointed:

liam: I can pick up Sat night primary (covering the rollout). I can’t do Sun — travelling. @chen can you take Sun primary? otherwise we need to rotate/hand off in the middle of the weekend.

chen: I can do Sun primary but only after 00:00 UTC — have a meeting earlier. will need a clear handoff checklist + the rollout notes. can someone paste the runbook link?

sophie: I’m secondary both nights. adding runbook links in thread. also pinging @pagerduty-bot to create a temporary escalation rule so alerts go to liam/chen directly.

pagerduty-bot: Escalation update: temporary routing applied. Primary (Sat): liam, Secondary: sophie. Primary (Sun): chen, Secondary: sophie. Notifying on-call mobiles.

maria: thank you all. handoff checklist (quick):
- confirm primary/secondary in PD
- verify scheduled deploy job id and canary steps
- snapshot current traffic baselines (qps, p95)
- open bridge if any paging during rollout
- post customer-impact notes to #incidents if >P2

sophie: paste of rollout job and runbook:
- Rollout job: infra/cicd/jobs/model-rollout/2026-04-10-22
- Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/model-rollout-and-rollback
- Paging runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/paging/inference-500s

liam: got the links. quick note on canary: we shift 5%->25%->100% over 30m with automatic health checks (latency+error). if p50>300ms or 5xx spike >1% cancel and rollback.

(5 minutes later)

ops-runbook-bot: Incident monitor: spike detected — 5xx increasing in prod in EU region. Threshold crossed: 0.8% -> 1.6% over 3m. Triggering incident channel and paging primary.

pagerduty-bot: Paging liam (primary Sat). Incident created: INC-20260410-8422. Severity: P1 (customer errors). Bridge: https://meet.redwood/incident/INC-20260410-8422

liam: I’m on the bridge. quick summary: 5xx spike started ~22:05 UTC, correlated with model rollout canary stage. rolling back canary to previous variant now.

chen: noted. which customers impacted? ops dashboard shows top callers: app-eu-prod and analytics-proxy. app-eu-prod error rate up 4x.

sophie: customer impact assessment: 8 customers with >5% error rate, 24 customers with transient increases. major customers: acme-inc (SLA), andora (page sent to AM). marking high-touch customers.

liam: mitigation steps I’m doing now:
1) pause rollout pipeline (ci-stop job)
2) revert canary to stable model (deploy rollback command)
3) scale inference pool to +1 node to absorb tail latency

liam: running commands:
```
# pause pipeline
curl -X POST https://ci.internal/api/jobs/infra/cicd/jobs/model-rollout/2026-04-10-22/pause -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'

# revert canary
kubectl -n inference set image deploy/model-serving model=image:stable-20260330

# add node
redwoodctl pool scale --pool inference-eu --add-nodes 1
```

ops-runbook-bot: Action logged. Rolling restart triggered for canary replicaset.

(7 minutes)

liam: errors dropping from 1.6% -> 0.4% p95 latency improving. still watching for regressions. opening an incident postmortem PR and assigning owners.

sophie: filing P1 template into #incidents -> will include customer list and who to notify.

maria: small note for handoff: if liam needs to hand off to chen mid-incident, use the bridge and run through "Handoff script" in runbook. key things to confirm: current mitigation, commands executed, and whether rollback is complete.

liam: thanks. Chen — if you’re taking Sun primary, please review the rollback steps and the canary thresholds. I’ll leave the incident bridge open for 30m and then handoff summary before I step off.

chen: will do. quick question — do we have a safe auto-fallback policy for the private tenants during rollouts? i remember a routing rule that sends traffic to hosted fallback when model fails.

sophie: yes — Smart routing has a fallback: model-variant=fallback-hosted. that is enabled for high-risk customers. checking now: fallback active for acme-inc andora.

liam: post-incident summary (to paste in #incidents):
- timeline: 22:05 error spike during canary, 22:07 rollout paused, 22:09 rollback initiated, 22:15 errors declined to baseline.
- root cause: canary model introduced tokenization edge-case causing 5xx for a subset of sharded requests.
- mitigation: pause + rollback + scale; fallback routing served high-touch customers.
- next steps: add canary end-to-end test for sharded requests; tighten canary health check thresholds.

chen: ack. i’ll take ownership of the postmortem tasks for the EMEA region tomorrow (add test + adjust thresholds). also will pick up Sun primary: will be in at 00:15 UTC, will check logs and pipeline status.

liam: thanks @chen. sophie — please keep secondary until 06:00 UTC.

sophie: will do. adding a short handoff note so the Sun primary has context:
- Handoff note: rollback done, pool scaled +1, bridge still up (https://meet.redwood/incident/INC-20260410-8422), incident PR: https://git.internal/redwood/pm/incidents/INC-20260410-8422
- Checkpoints: verify pd rules, confirm no further 5xx spikes for 30m, validate canary tests added to CI.

maria: really appreciate everyone stepping in. this is a good example of the oncall handoff process working. if anything else pops up ping in-thread and on the bridge. :heart:

(30m later)

liam: closing the bridge — will hand off a short note to chen in PD and leave the incident post open for postmortem.

pagerduty-bot: Handoff message posted to chen. Current oncall for Sun primary confirmed: chen.

chen: received handoff. I’ll do a full check at 00:20 UTC and post anything unusual. thanks all.

sophie: ending my secondary watch at 06:00 UTC unless we need to extend. good job team :thumbsup:

maria: logging this handoff in the weekend coverage doc: https://docs.redwood/oncall/weekend-coverages/2026-04. Lovely coordination.
